title: Build a Complete HTML Website
subtitle: A short practical refresher followed by 20 new application questions
description: Review the ten HTML dashboard topics. Includes three capstone examples and exactly two fresh review questions from each of Lessons 1–10.

blocks.text: Welcome to the HTML final review. This lesson is intentionally shorter on new theory and longer on practical decisions. You will revisit the ten dashboard topics and answer two new application questions for each lesson, for exactly 20 questions.

Start by reading the requirement, tracing where its data comes from, and deciding what success should look like. Then test both a normal case and a boundary or failure case. A correct program should not only work once; it should behave predictably when its inputs change.

Practice direction: Open Home → Menu → Practical/Practice → select HTML. Paste this snippet into the matching web/React editor, run or preview it, and compare what happens. Then change one value or element and run it again so you can observe the effect. If this course is not available in the in-app runner, use a suitable compiler or interpreter for the language.

blocks.text: Use the third example as a starting point, then explain how it relates to the course topic: Complete your HTML journey by building a practical website and reviewing the major concepts.

Answer two questions from each dashboard lesson. These questions are newly written for this review and are not copied from the corresponding lesson quizzes. Read carefully: select the option that best satisfies the requirement, not merely an option that could work in a different situation.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 1 — Introduction to HTML: A team receives a repository with no run instructions. What should the maintainer add to make a fresh setup verifiable?
options: A setup/run guide plus a minimal test or sample command.
Only a screenshot of the editor.
A statement that setup is obvious.
blocks.explanation: A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A reproducible setup guide helps another developer validate the project from a clean start.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 1 — Introduction to HTML: The app works after manual edits but fails when built from source. What should be compared?
options: The actual source, compiler/runtime configuration, and documented build path.
blocks.explanation: Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Build and runtime configuration are part of a reproducible program, not separate from it.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 2 — HTML Text and Headings: A screen-reader user navigates by headings. What is the most useful structure?
options: A logical heading hierarchy that reflects the content.
Heading levels chosen only for font size.
blocks.explanation: Semantic heading hierarchy creates a navigable outline.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Semantic heading hierarchy creates a navigable outline.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Semantic heading hierarchy creates a navigable outline.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 2 — HTML Text and Headings: A page uses bold text to represent the title of every section. What should change?
options: Keep it bold but hide it.
Use real heading elements and style them with CSS.
Put every title inside an input.
blocks.explanation: Headings should use heading elements so structure is exposed beyond visual styling.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Headings should use heading elements so structure is exposed beyond visual styling.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Headings should use heading elements so structure is exposed beyond visual styling.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 3 — Links and Navigation: A navigation link points to a file whose case differs from the deployed file name. What should the developer check?
options: Whether it is inside a section.
The exact relative path and filename in the deployed environment.
blocks.explanation: Paths can be case-sensitive in production and should match the deployed resource.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Paths can be case-sensitive in production and should match the deployed resource.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Paths can be case-sensitive in production and should match the deployed resource.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 3 — Links and Navigation: A control saves the current form rather than navigating to a page. Which semantic control is best?
options: A heading styled like a link.
An img with no alt text.
A button that describes the save action.
blocks.explanation: A button is the appropriate semantic control for an action.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A button is the appropriate semantic control for an action.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A button is the appropriate semantic control for an action.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 4 — Images and Multimedia: A tutorial video has no captions and contains essential spoken steps. What is the most useful accessibility improvement?
options: Add accurate captions or a transcript.
Make the video file name longer.
blocks.explanation: Captions and transcripts make spoken content available to more users.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Captions and transcripts make spoken content available to more users.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Captions and transcripts make spoken content available to more users.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 4 — Images and Multimedia: A decorative background image is announced by a screen reader even though it adds no information. What should be considered?
options: Describe every pixel in a long alt.
Mark it decorative with an empty alt when implemented as an img.
Turn it into a required input.
Put its filename in a heading.
blocks.explanation: Decorative images should not add redundant announcements.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Decorative images should not add redundant announcements.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Decorative images should not add redundant announcements.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 5 — HTML Lists and Tables: A report table has several columns but no labels identifying each column. What should be added?
options: Proper table header cells and, where useful, a caption.
blocks.explanation: Headers establish the meaning of values in each column/row.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Headers establish the meaning of values in each column/row.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Headers establish the meaning of values in each column/row.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 5 — HTML Lists and Tables: A nested set of topics is presented as a table purely to align indentation. What is more appropriate?
options: A nested list reflecting the hierarchy.
blocks.explanation: Lists communicate grouped or nested items; tables are for tabular relationships.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Lists communicate grouped or nested items; tables are for tabular relationships.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Lists communicate grouped or nested items; tables are for tabular relationships.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 6 — HTML Forms: A form’s browser validation passes, but an API receives a crafted invalid request. What must the API do?
options: Validate all relevant fields on the server independently.
Accept all values from hidden fields.
blocks.explanation: Client validation can be bypassed; trusted server code must enforce requirements.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Client validation can be bypassed; trusted server code must enforce requirements.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Client validation can be bypassed; trusted server code must enforce requirements.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 6 — HTML Forms: A form has two buttons, and the “Preview” button unexpectedly submits. What should be reviewed?
options: The button type and intended submit behavior.
blocks.explanation: A button inside a form may submit by default; explicit type avoids surprises.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A button inside a form may submit by default; explicit type avoids surprises.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A button inside a form may submit by default; explicit type avoids surprises.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 7 — Semantic HTML: A screen includes the main lesson, related recommendations, and site navigation. Which structure helps assistive technology identify them?
options: A table used as a layout grid.
Meaningful nav, main, and aside/section landmarks where appropriate.
blocks.explanation: Semantic landmarks identify major page regions.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Semantic landmarks identify major page regions.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Semantic landmarks identify major page regions.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 7 — Semantic HTML: A self-contained tutorial post can be shared independently of surrounding links. Which element may express that content?
blocks.explanation: Article suits a self-contained composition such as an independent post or lesson.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Article suits a self-contained composition such as an independent post or lesson.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Article suits a self-contained composition such as an independent post or lesson.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 8 — HTML5 and Modern Web Structure: A page should expand to the device width on mobile. Which setup is essential to verify?
options: The viewport meta declaration alongside responsive styles.
blocks.explanation: Viewport configuration and responsive CSS let the page adapt to mobile dimensions.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Viewport configuration and responsive CSS let the page adapt to mobile dimensions.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Viewport configuration and responsive CSS let the page adapt to mobile dimensions.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 8 — HTML5 and Modern Web Structure: A disclosure section needs simple native show/hide behavior. Which elements are a good fit?
blocks.explanation: The details/summary pair provides native disclosure behavior.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. The details/summary pair provides native disclosure behavior.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. The details/summary pair provides native disclosure behavior.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 9 — Accessible and Professional HTML: A user cannot tell which item has keyboard focus. What should the site do?
options: Make focus visible only on hover.
Provide a clear visible focus indicator.
Make every control inaccessible to keyboard users.
blocks.explanation: Visible focus is essential for keyboard navigation.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Visible focus is essential for keyboard navigation.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Visible focus is essential for keyboard navigation.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 9 — Accessible and Professional HTML: A form field uses placeholder text as the only label. What needs improvement?
blocks.explanation: Labels remain available while users enter information and programmatically identify the input.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Labels remain available while users enter information and programmatically identify the input.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Labels remain available while users enter information and programmatically identify the input.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 10 — Build a Complete HTML Website: The final project passes one example input. What is the strongest completion check?
options: Stop testing as soon as the screen appears.
Remove error handling to reduce lines.
Test normal, boundary, empty, and failure cases and document how to run it.
blocks.explanation: Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Broader tests and reproducible setup provide stronger evidence than one happy-path example.

blocks.question: Review from Lesson 10 — Build a Complete HTML Website: A teammate cannot reproduce the project’s behavior. What is likely missing?
options: Repeatable instructions, clear dependencies, and a testable expected result.
blocks.explanation: Reproducibility requires enough source and setup information for another person to verify the same behavior.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Reproducibility requires enough source and setup information for another person to verify the same behavior.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Reproducibility requires enough source and setup information for another person to verify the same behavior.
